caption:
Can two AI detectors be better than one? Superhuman acquires GPTZero

Superhuman, a company formed when Grammarly bought email provider Superhuman, has acquired GPTZero, a three-year-old AI detection startup. GPTZero was built by Princeton grad Edward Tian as a senior thesis project.

GPTZero has amassed more than 19 million registered users and $30 million in annual recurring revenue. The company was profitable in 2024, according to Tian.

Superhuman already had an AI detection tool built into its platform, but says 'two AI detectors are better than one.'

GPTZero's mission has been to help humans detect and defend against AI slop, while Grammarly's tool helps users determine whether their writing appears AI-generated.
